findings.review_scope: Registered-source review of High-dimensional covariance matrices under dynamic volatility models: Asymptotics and shrinkage estimation by Yi Ding and Xinghua Zheng. The fixed 49-page PDF is arXiv:2211.10203v2, with margin date 21 November 2022 and title-page date 18 November 2022. Main text and references end on page 36. Numbered Section 5, Proof of Theorem 3, remains main text. The Supplement Materials notice on pages 32-33 is not the attached supplement; only the supplement title on page 37 was inspected, in a crop ending at y=143.
findings.inventory: Five bold SFBX1200 Theorem headings occur on pages 7,8,10,12,13, numbered 1-5. Every complete theorem statement was compared with its rendered source page. Fresh enumeration covers pages 1-36, separately confirms the four-part Assumption 1 on page 6 and excludes ordinary theorem mentions, the Section 5 proof heading, Corollary 1 and Remarks.
original_statements: Theorem 1 retains model (1.1), all of Assumption 1, the eta-to-zero regime and the Levy-distance conclusion between the dynamic and coupled iid sample spectral distributions.

Theorem 2 retains eta>c for a fixed positive constant, existence of positive delta and the eventual expected spectral-second-moment gap. It is not a samplewise inequality, stochastic dominance or a Levy-distance separation claim.

Theorem 3 retains delta<min(a_p,b_p)<a_p+b_p<1-delta, divergence of M_p, M_p=o(sqrt(p)) and Levy convergence between adjusted and iid sample spectral laws. It does not assert that adjusted observations are iid.

Theorem 4 retains every inherited and additional hypothesis, positive bounded limiting support with h1<=h2, bounded g with finitely many discontinuities and convergence for each z in the upper half-plane. Its complete limiting integral retains both printed y inverse factors rather than substituting the y coefficient from equation (2.9).

Theorem 5 retains the reference to all assumptions of Theorem 4 and the p^{-1/2}-normalized Frobenius difference between the estimated NLS matrix and the separate infeasible oracle. It does not state consistency to the unconditional covariance matrix itself.
source_passages: All 24 source entries and 12 auxiliary passages were compared with rendered main-text pages. The covariance recursion, barred unconditional covariance, innovation representation and coupled iid comparator preserve their distinct roles. The comparator uses the same z_t; the source endpoint T and covariance endpoint n remain as printed.

The four Assumption 1 clauses retain Gaussian innovations, a nonnegative population covariance with nonzero limiting ESD, a spectral upper bound and p/n tending to positive y. They do not impose a positive lower eigenvalue bound on every population matrix. Matrix order, square root, spectral and Frobenius norms and ESD conventions match pages 5-6.
The Levy formula, unnamed eta formula with sqrt(p(1-a-b)) inside its minimum, two regimes and empirical second-moment definitions match pages 7-8. The expectation operator remains ordinary italic E.

The marginal GARCH variance recursion, random single-coordinate QMLE, exact parameter domain, projection identity coefficient and all lag weights match page 9 and its continuation. The enlarged QMLE crop confirms the printed positive objective with argmax. No pooling, stationary initialization or tie-selection rule is inserted.

Adjusted returns use the inverse square root of P_t; the adjusted covariance is an uncentered average divided by n. The complete Stieltjes and Marchenko-Pastur formulas on page 10, population eigenvalue notation, spectral functional calculus, generalized ESD, eigenvector convention and resolvent trace on pages 11-12 remain distinct. The generalized ESD divides by trace(g(Sigma)), while the resolvent trace divides by p.

Clipping uses min(lambda,L) and preserves eigenvectors. The NLS construction invokes Ledoit and Wolf (2015); its missing numerical construction is explicitly unresolved. The oracle is separately defined by (2.13). The enlarged oracle crop confirms the zero-eigenvalue branch for y>1, ordinary square without modulus bars, underlined companion F, companion formula and unindexed boundary-value notation.
findings.corrections: Rendered page 10 revealed two errors in existing original-source prose. D18 omitted H in from F is determined by H in that its Stieltjes transform; auxiliary A12 changed has the same LSD to shares the same LSD. Both source phrasings are restored. The theorem inventory and dependency graph are unchanged. Prior JSON artifacts and extraction scripts are archived under review-history/before-stieltjes-prose-correction/. The enlarged stieltjes-context.png records the corrected source wording.
findings.dependency_review: All 30 direct uses, 61 related theorem connections and 24 local dependency lists were checked. The first two Theorems retain their distinct eta regimes and conclusions; the MP transform is not needed by their statement definitions. Adjustment-dependent results reach the actual QMLE, marginal recursion, projection and inverse-square-root return construction. Theorem 4 reaches functional calculus and the explicit generalized resolvent. Theorem 5 retains the inherited support and g hypotheses but not Theorem 4 generalized-transform conclusion. Its oracle reaches the clipped spectrum and limiting transform, not the external NLS algorithm. The generalized ESD and proof-only external results remain contextual rather than invented prerequisites.
findings.names_and_highlights: Each interface has source-derived natural-language terminology, source kind and heading, matching selectors and same-paper relationship explanations. The unnamed eta formula remains an auxiliary passage rather than receiving an invented name. The source projection-matrix name is preserved without inferring idempotence. Assumption 1, theorem-excerpt conditions and definitions remain distinguishable.
findings.source_limitations: All 27 existing source issues are retained: source dates and boundary, barred covariance and coupling, T/n endpoints, population degeneracy allowance, eta scaling, expectation-only conclusion, QMLE sign and coordinate choice, parameter-domain mismatch, missing initialization and selection, projection terminology and presample observations, covariance normalization, y versus inverse-y, generalized-measure normalization and possible signed/zero weights, g outside limiting support, pointwise z quantification, unspecified clipping threshold, external NLS construction, oracle zero boundary cases, ordinary versus modulus square, companion and boundary shorthand, inherited g condition and external proof citations. No mathematical repair or proof certification is claimed.
findings.validation: Both independent census validators pass. The corrected six artifacts reproduce byte for byte in an empty directory. Source identity, page count, dates, authors, fresh text on all permitted pages, heading enumeration, complete theorem evidence, every direct and local dependency list, every related path, source kinds, keyword and selector occurrences, historical hashes and the two correction locations were checked. Rebuilding uses the verified fixed PDF plus saved extraction and does not itself perform a semantic review.
